comment:
Concerns / changes: I would encourage the guidance to operationalize meaningful human oversight more explicitly as a behavioural and organizational capability, rather than primarily as the presence of a human reviewer. Effective oversight requires that people can detect potential errors, question AI recommendations, understand uncertainty, resist inappropriate deference, and meaningfully override or escalate decisions when necessary. Evaluation should therefore consider trust calibration, automation bias, perceived model authority, workload, and actual override behaviour, in addition to technical model performance.

For conversational and mental health related AI, I would also recommend attention to psychosocial risks that can affect human agency, including perceived empathy, emotional reliance, and excessive epistemic dependence on an AI system. These factors may influence whether users and professionals continue to exercise independent judgement even when formal human oversight mechanisms are present. Explicitly incorporating these behavioural dimensions would strengthen the guidance for high impact and vulnerable user contexts.
